title: Electrophysiological Studies of MIN6 Cells
author: Kiichi Hirota
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.v68e9hw

steps.title: Incubate MIN6 cells in glucose solution
steps.instruction: Incubate MIN6 cells in an extracellular bath solution containing 2 mM glucose for 30 min at 37 °C before patch‑clamp experiments.

steps.title: Prepare patch pipettes and electrodes
steps.instruction: Use patch pipettes (G‑1.5; Narishige, Tokyo, Japan) with a resistance of 5–7 MΩ when filled with pipette solution, and correct the membrane potential for the liquid‑junction potential at the tip of the patch pipette in KRBH buffer; also correct the indifferent reference electrode (filled with KRBH buffer and placed in the bath) for its liquid‑junction potential.

substeps.instruction: Select patch pipettes (G‑1.5; Narishige) and fill them with the appropriate internal solution; verify resistance of 5–7 MΩ.
Measure and apply liquid‑junction potential correction for the pipette tip in KRBH buffer.
Measure and apply liquid‑junction potential correction for the reference electrode filled with KRBH buffer in the bath.

steps.title: Record membrane potential and whole‑cell current
steps.instruction: Connect the EPC 800 patch‑clamp amplifier (HEKA Elektronik, Holliston, MA, USA) driven by Clampex 9 (Axon Instruments, Union City, CA, USA) to deliver voltage‑step protocols and digitize current; compensate the capacitance transient current with the amplifier; whole‑cell capacitance is 7.4 ± 1.5 pF and series resistance (Rs) is 13.3 ± 1.3 MΩ (n = 6); do not electronically compensate Rs and do not correct reported potentials for Rs.

steps.title: Filter and sample current signals
steps.instruction: Filter the whole‑cell current at 1 kHz using an internal four‑pole Bessel filter, sample the filtered signal at 2 kHz, and transfer the digital data through a Digidata 1322A (Axon Instruments).

steps.title: Analyze recorded currents
steps.instruction: Perform subsequent current analysis using Clampfit 9 (Axon Instruments).
